DIS.rationale: Disney presents a mixed picture. The franchise is genuinely world-class — dominant parks (140M visitors, $2.6B segment OI in Q2), a streaming business that has crossed the profitability inflection (SVOD OI +88% YoY, 10.6% margins for the first time), and unmatched IP. However, the quantitative earnings trajectory is deteriorating: GAAP EPS fell -29.8% YoY to $1.27 despite +6.5% revenue growth, as below-the-line costs expanded sharply. Operating income is flat at $4.6B despite top-line gains, revealing margin compression. Valuation at 14.4x PE is at the floor of its 12-month range (12.5–23.8x), but this discount is earned by the earnings decline, not a dislocation. The qualitative report's forward guidance (12% adjusted EPS growth for FY2026, double-digit into FY2027) and the $60B parks CapEx commitment provide a credible forward-looking offset to the backward-looking deterioration, but the gap between adjusted ($1.57) and GAAP ($1.27) EPS in Q2 is wide and raises questions about what 'adjusted' excludes. The balance sheet is sound (equity $115.3B, leverage 0.78x) and the latest quarter's OCF ($6.91B) is strong. Net-net: a high-quality franchise in a temporary earnings trough, trading at a historically low multiple, but without clear evidence that GAAP earnings have bottomed. The near-term catalyst (Q2 beat + guidance) is already priced in given the stock's stabilization around $100. Score reflects mild fundamental attractiveness from franchise quality and valuation floor, tempered by earnings deterioration and the adjusted-vs-GAAP gap.
key_factors: GAAP EPS declined -29.8% YoY to $1.27 in Q2 FY2026 (from $1.81), despite revenue growing +6.5% to $25.17B — below-the-line costs expanding materially
Operating income flat at $4.60B (vs $4.44B YoY) while revenue grew 6.5%, indicating margin compression; operating margin 17.7%
Adjusted EPS of $1.57 beat consensus by 5.4% — the $0.30 gap vs GAAP $1.27 raises questions about what adjustments exclude
PE diluted at 14.4x (2026-06-11), near floor of 12-month range 12.5–23.8x; P/B at 1.54x vs 2.1x peak — discount is earned by earnings decline
Streaming inflection: SVOD operating income surged 88% YoY to $582M with 10.6% margins, first double-digit margin quarter
Experiences segment delivered $2.6B operating income in Q2; 140M global park visitors in 2023, 2x runner-up Universal
Management guided 12% adjusted EPS growth for FY2026 with double-digit growth into FY2027; $60B parks CapEx over 10 years; buyback target lifted to $8B
Balance sheet strengthening: equity $115.3B (up from $106.7B), leverage 0.78x; Q2 OCF $6.91B strong but Q1 OCF only $735M — highly lumpy
Macro headwinds: 10Y Treasury 4.45%, oil $91.58/bbl (parks cost pressure), Baa corporate yields 6.0% (refinancing cost on debt)
Comcast's Epic Universe showing strong growth (revenue +19-24% YoY) but operational issues (worst-rated Florida park on TripAdvisor) — Disney moat intact near-term
